reviews.summary: The collection already has a coherent forest-and-paper identity. A compact editorial hierarchy could give the actual trail choices and route data more prominence while keeping loading and recovery states clearly distinct. These are visual hypotheses, not usability scores.

observations.issue: The large two-line hero heading fills much of the upper screen, and its supporting text begins close to the last line.
observations.suggestion: Reduce the headline footprint and add separation before the subtitle, bringing the featured trail higher.

observations.issue: The route map dominates the detail page while the useful distance, time and pace appear in one visually uniform block.
observations.suggestion: Balance map height with a compact, aligned information strip and retain both preparation and saving actions.

observations.issue: The progress label sits close to the bottom of the bar, while Connection help is visually faint relative to the main recovery button.
observations.suggestion: Add spacing around progress feedback and make the secondary help action legible while preserving the loading state.

observations.issue: Both trail rows repeat the same landscape thumbnail and have large text/illustration blocks.
observations.suggestion: Use coherent but distinct illustrated crops and tighter information alignment to make the two trails easier to scan.

direction.name: A quiet field journal
direction.typography: An editorial serif headline with crisp sans-serif controls and trail metadata.
principles: Preserve existing actions and state distinctions.
Give trail choices and route data priority over decorative headings.
Use one shared visual language across ordinary, loading and recovery states.

prompts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one polished portrait mobile UI screenshot, edge to edge, no device frame, no perspective, no montage. Image 1 is the target state to redesign; other images are context from the same Fieldnotes app. Audience: beginner weekend walkers planning short coastal trails. Shared direction: a quiet outdoor field journal, warm ivory #F5F3EA, deep forest #183F34, muted sage #7C927D, restrained lime #D9EDAA and small ochre route markers. Crisp contemporary sans serif for controls, editorial serif only for the main headline. Preserve the original actions, content and selected navigation state. Use comfortable text contrast and a clear 8-point rhythm; compact the oversized heading area, give the important trail information more hierarchy, and keep generous breathing room. Use a richer original flat landscape illustration with fine contour lines; no invented photos, ratings, memberships or new product features. Keep all supplied copy readable and accurate. Target: Home. Retain fieldnotes branding, MAKE ROOM FOR OUTSIDE, A little more outside., the two supporting sentences, Cerro Azul loop with 4.8 km, Easy and 1 h 20 min, its open-arrow action, A good day to wander, weather 21 degrees with Clear skies, light breeze and water reminder. Retain bottom navigation Home, Explore, Saved, You with Home selected. Make the landscape trail card the visual anchor; use a more compact weather row and a rounded forest-green arrow button. Render at roughly the source tall phone aspect ratio with safe-area status bar and home indicator.
